title: test(plugin-approvals): pin the two managerIsProvablyOutsideOrg screens to equal verdicts
body:
Part of #11286

`sys_user.manager_id` carries **two independent organization screens, in two packages, with no shared code**, and nothing enforced the mirroring they were written with. This adds the cross-referencing contract test that pins them to the **same verdicts on the same fixture matrix**.

| package | entry point | screen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plugin-approvals` | `ApprovalService.lookupManager` (#10153) | `managerIsProvablyOutsideOrg` — private method |
| `plugin-sharing` | `TeamGraphService.managerOf`, `BusinessUnitGraphService.managerOf` (#10231) | `managerIsProvablyOutsideOrg` — module function |

## ⚠️ This PR PINS the duplication. It does not remove it.

Collapsing the two into shared code is a **cross-package dependency decision** and is deliberately out of scope here. #7497 — does approver routing imply record read visibility? — is open precisely on whether these two questions should converge at all, and fusing the implementations would prejudge it. **The removal question stays open.**

One correction to the finding's own text, measured on `main`: it says "`plugin-approvals` already depends on `plugin-sharing`, so the direction exists". It does **not** — `plugin-approvals/package.json` lists neither a dependency nor a devDependency on `plugin-sharing`. That makes the shared-helper option strictly more expensive than the card assumed, and is worth knowing before the removal question is decided.

## Predicted first, then measured

The verdict for every row was derived by reading both implementations **before the file was first run** — that prediction is what makes a divergence a finding rather than a surprise. `true` = "provably outside the organization" ⇒ drop the manager; `false` = leave routing/sharing exactly as it was.

| row | fixture (`sys_member` rows for `u_mgr`) | org arg | predicted | measured `plugin-sharing` | measured `plugin-approvals` | agree |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | `[org_b]` | `undefined` | false | false | false | ✅ |
| R2 | `[org_b]` | `null` | false | false | false | ✅ |
| R3 | `[org_b]` | `''` | false | false | false | ✅ |
| R4 | (no rows at all) | `org_a` | false | false | false | ✅ |
| R5 | rows for **another user** only, in `org_b` | `org_a` | false | false | false | ✅ |
| R6 | `[org_b]` | `org_a` | **true** | **true** | **true** | ✅ |
| R7 | `[org_b, org_c]` | `org_a` | **true** | **true** | **true** | ✅ |
| R8 | `[org_a]` | `org_a` | false | false | false | ✅ |
| R9 | `[org_b, org_a]` | `org_a` | false | false | false | ✅ |
| R10 | `[organization_id: null]` | `org_a` | false | false | false | ✅ |
| R11 | `[organization_id: '']` | `org_a` | false | false | false | ✅ |
| R12 | `[null, org_b]` | `org_a` | **true** | **true** | **true** | ✅ |
| R13 | `[null, org_a]` | `org_a` | false | false | false | ✅ |
| R14 | the read **throws** | `org_a` | false | false | false | ✅ |
| R15 | the read returns `undefined` | `org_a` | false | false | false | ✅ |
| R16 | the read returns `null` | `org_a` | false | false | false | ✅ |
| R17 | `[organization_id: 7]` (number) | `'7'` | false | false | false | ✅ |
| R18 | `[organization_id: 7]` (number) | `'8'` | **true** | **true** | **true** | ✅ |
| R19 | 1200 rows, caller-org row at index **999** | `org_a` | false | false | false | ✅ |
| R20 | 1200 rows, caller-org row at index **1100** | `org_a` | **true** | **true** | **true** | ✅ |

**The two screens agree on all 20 rows. Measured matrix == predicted matrix, exactly.** The card anticipated a possible divergence; there is none on this tree. What the pin buys is that a future one-sided edit cannot land quietly.

Rows R4/R5/R10/R11/R14/R15/R16 are the **absent-tenancy fail-open** posture; R6/R7/R12 are the **cross-org manager**; R8/R9/R13/R17/R18 are the **`sys_member` shapes**; R19/R20 bracket the declared `limit: 1000` from both directions.

Three read-shape differences are expressed as **verdict** differences rather than asserted directly, because the fixture double applies `where` and projects `fields`:

- a side that stopped asking for `organization_id` reads `undefined` and fails open while the other screens out (R6/R8);
- a side that dropped the `user_id` predicate sees another user's rows (R5);
- a narrower `limit` flips R19, a wider one flips R20.

No read shape is asserted **directly** — that would be a wider pin than this card, so the recorded reads are logged as diagnostics only.

## The test can fail — measured on both arms

A parity test that passes on its first run deserves suspicion, so each screen was ablated **separately**: a test that only ever exercised one arm would still go red under a single mutation.

| leg | mutation | on-disk confirmation | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | none (baseline) | — | **21 passed** |
| 1 | `plugin-sharing`: `if (!orgs.length) return false` → `return true` (fail-**closed**) | old literal 1→0, marker 0→1, mutated line printed from disk | **6 failed** — exactly R4, R5, R10, R11, R15, R16 |
| 2 | `plugin-approvals`: `if (orgs.includes(requestOrg))` → `if (!orgs.includes(...))` | old literal 1→0, marker 0→1, mutated line printed from disk | **10 failed** — exactly R6, R7, R8, R9, R12, R13, R17, R18, R19, R20 |
| 3 | restored | `git hash-object` == HEAD blob on both files | **21 passed** |

Both red sets were the ones predicted for those mutations. Restoration was proved by `git hash-object` against the HEAD blob (`9d7edec4…` sharing, `4396ac0b…` approvals), from an absolute path with `git -C`, treating an empty hash as failure — not by a `trap` having fired.

**No rebuild was needed between legs, and that is the point:** both screens are reached by **relative source path**, so nothing resolves through a `dist/` artifact and the mutation reaches the executed code directly. The red/green transition is itself the proof.

*(The first attempt at leg 1 was a silent no-op — a `/` in the replacement text terminated perl's `s///` program early. The on-disk literal counts caught it and the leg was re-run properly; it is recorded here rather than quietly retried.)*

## Why the cross-package declaration

plugin-sharing's screen is reached by **relative source path**, and that is the only way in: it is deliberately **not** exported from that package's index (exporting it would hoist a security screen into another plugin's public API surface — the very decision this card is fenced out of), and the package publishes `.` only, so there is no subpath to import.

That read escapes the package, so it is declared in `CROSS_PACKAGE_TEST_INPUTS` and mirrored into turbo.json's `@objectstack/plugin-approvals#test` `inputs`. Without **both**, a change to the sharing screen would never re-run this pin — the exact blind spot that gate exists for. One file, not `plugin-sharing/src/**`: nothing else in that package is read.

## No changeset — `skip-changeset`

This PR publishes nothing: one test file, one gate declaration, and turbo `inputs`. Per `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs`, a PR that releases nothing takes the **`skip-changeset` label**, and an empty-frontmatter changeset is rejected outright (it is a real input to `changesets/action` and an all-empty set stalls the release silently and greenly, #4898). The label is applied.

## Verification — all at `44c46aa213`, the head of this branch

```
pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run
      src/manager-org-screen-parity.contract.test.ts      Tests  21 passed (21)
pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals test          Tests  606 passed (606)  (32 files)
pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck     tsc --noEmit, clean
```

Gate union re-run on this commit — every one green, quoting each gate's own verdict line:

- `check:cross-package-test-inputs` — `OK: 16 package(s) read outside themselves, all declared, and turbo.json hashes every declared glob.`
- `check:where-matcher` — `293 matcher(s) discovered, 293 answer the combinator battery correctly or refuse it loudly (181 refuse). 0 silently-wrong`
- `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:slot-lookup`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:type-source-resolution`, `check:published-files`, `check:pnpm-filter-targets`, `check:entry-guard`, `check:parse-guard`, `check:i18n`, `check-plugin-teardown-shape`, `check-ci-filter-parity` — all exit 0.

`check:where-matcher` went red on the first run and was repaired, not silenced: the fixture's `matchesWhere` read a combinator as a field name. It now **refuses** the shapes it does not model. Because both screens wrap their read in `catch { return false }`, a bare throw would be swallowed into a fail-open verdict on *both* sides — parity green while the fixture asserted nothing — so the refusal is recorded in a collector and asserted empty before any verdict is read.

`check:i18n` initially reported `PREREQUISITE NOT MET — the workspace CLI is not built`. That is **not measured**, so the CLI was built and it was re-run: `OK (9 package(s) — all bundles in sync)`.

**Not measured locally:** `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` (needs the full workspace closure built — repo-wide, left to CI), and the repo-wide `pnpm lint`. Both run in CI regardless.

⛔ Not flipped ready, not enqueued, no auto-merge — landing is the dispatching seat's window.
